State what would trigger a change to the plan and what the host should communicate when actual conditions differ.
manager_check: A seating plan must respect whole-restaurant capacity; an open table is not automatically usable capacity.

title: EVERY-STATION READINESS EXCEPTION PLAN
prompt:
Review this pre-service readiness evidence for every operating station.

Stations: [host / servers / bussers / bar / expo / line / prep / pizza / salad / dish]
Opening checks and verified condition by station: [paste]
Unfinished prep, low product, equipment issues, training gaps, or call-outs: [list]
Expected demand and timing: [facts]

Do not rewrite a generic opening checklist. Create an exception plan showing only what is outside standard, the guest or operating consequence, the temporary control, the accountable owner, the deadline, the escalation trigger, and the proof needed before the exception can be considered closed. Separate critical blockers from conditions the team can safely manage during service.
manager_check: Keep permanent station checklists in their controlled source; use this prompt only for verified exceptions and decisions.

title: PRE-SHIFT PLAN TRANSFER AUDIT
prompt:
Audit whether this pre-shift meeting actually transferred the operating plan to the team.

Manager plan: [paste concise plan]
Pre-shift talking points used: [paste]
Station-specific changes or exceptions: [list]
Questions employees asked: [notes]
Observed execution during the first service wave: [facts]

Identify what the team clearly understood, what remained vague, which roles did not receive the information they needed, and whether owners, triggers, and escalation paths were explicit. Produce a corrected five-minute transfer outline for the next shift and no more than three verification questions a manager can ask employees to confirm understanding.
manager_check: Attendance does not prove transfer; verify that each role can explain the plan and its decision triggers.

title: CONTINGENCY TRIGGER & PRESSURE RESPONSE BUILDER
prompt:
Turn these known service risks into predefined contingency triggers and responses.

Expected demand: [facts]
Known risks: [call-outs / reservation wave / equipment / product / weather / new employees / other]
Current staffing and station capacity: [facts]
Available manager authority and backup resources: [facts]

For each material risk, define: early warning signal, measurable trigger where possible, immediate response, person authorized to act, communication path, guest-protection step, conditions for escalation, and evidence that shows the response worked. Avoid vague instructions such as “watch closely” or “use judgment” unless you define what the manager should observe.
manager_check: A contingency plan becomes useful only when the trigger, authority, and first action are clear before pressure arrives.

title: LIVE PLAN VARIANCE & NEXT-SHIFT ADVANTAGE
prompt:
Compare the shift plan with what actually happened and convert the difference into a next-shift advantage.

Planned demand, staffing, deployment, pacing, prep, and contingencies: [paste]
Actual conditions and timing: [facts]
Manager changes made during service: [facts]
Guest, team, ticket-time, product, and financial effects: [facts]
Open commitments: [list]

Separate forecast error, capacity error, readiness miss, execution miss, and unavoidable exception. Identify which live adjustments helped, which transferred pressure elsewhere, and what should change before the next comparable shift. End with one lesson to preserve, one controlled change to test, one owner, and the evidence required to verify improvement.
manager_check: Do not turn one unusual shift into a permanent standard without comparable evidence.

title: STANDARD DRINK CARD AUDIT
prompt:
Audit this beverage recipe or Standard Drink Card for operational and financial completeness.

Drink name and approved recipe: [ingredients / exact quantities / method]
Glassware, ice, garnish, presentation, and service standard: [details]
Current ingredient costs and purchase units: [data]
Selling price and POS name/button: [data]
Observed bartender variations: [facts]

Check for unclear measurements, missing yield assumptions, inconsistent build order, unpriced components, garnish or mixer omissions, unsupported substitutions, presentation gaps, and POS naming problems. Calculate only from the data provided. Produce a corrected-control checklist and list every fact management must verify before approving a new recipe version.
manager_check: The approved recipe version controls; AI may expose gaps but cannot invent pour sizes, costs, or responsible-service rules.

title: BEVERAGE RECIPE COST & CONTRIBUTION REVIEW
prompt:
Review this beverage item using both cost percentage and contribution dollars.

Recipe quantities and current unit costs: [data]
Garnish, mixer, batch-yield, and consumable costs: [data]
Selling price: [amount]
Units sold and sales mix: [data]
Preparation time, training difficulty, and service impact: [facts]

Calculate recipe cost, recipe beverage-cost percentage, and gross contribution dollars only where the inputs support them. Explain how an attractive cost percentage can still produce weak contribution and how a higher-cost item can still contribute well. Identify missing data, operational tradeoffs, and the next pricing, recipe, or menu-placement questions management should verify before changing the drink.
manager_check: Review guest value, brand fit, execution, and responsible service along with the calculation.

title: POUR-COST VARIANCE INVESTIGATION
prompt:
Help me investigate a beverage pour-cost variance without assuming theft or blaming the bar team.

Beverage sales by category: [data]
Actual product usage at cost: [data]
Theoretical product cost or recipe usage: [data]
Inventory counts and count method: [facts]
Purchases, transfers, waste, comps, spills, substitutions, and promotions: [data]
Recipe versions, POS mapping, and observed pour practice: [facts]

Quantify the verified variance, then rank the checks for count accuracy, purchase/transfer recording, recipe version, POS mapping, unrecorded waste or comps, portion drift, pricing/mix, and possible loss. Separate mathematical facts from hypotheses. Produce a neutral investigation sequence, the evidence needed at each step, and a stop point before any employee conclusion.
manager_check: A variance is an investigation target, not proof of misconduct.

title: BEVERAGE INVENTORY JUSTIFICATION & PRODUCT RATIONALIZATION
prompt:
Evaluate whether each beverage product still has a clear reason to occupy cash, shelf space, and training attention.

Product list, cost, and usable on hand: [data]
Menu Reach—the number of approved permanent uses: [data]
Recent demand and last meaningful use: [data]
Contribution value and guest/brand importance: [facts]
Cross-use, substitution, and responsible depletion options: [facts]

Classify each item as Core, Cross-Use, Seasonal, One-Drink Risk, Deplete, or Review. Explain the evidence, identify products with weak inventory justification, and propose controlled next steps such as menu use, approved feature, legal return, substitution, par change, depletion, or retirement. Do not recommend irresponsible promotion or automatic reordering.
manager_check: A product should not survive merely because it is already on the shelf or once appeared in a recipe.

title: BARTENDER RECIPE CONSISTENCY TRAINING PLAN
prompt:
Build a short verification-based training plan for the beverage standards below.

Approved Standard Drink Cards: [paste or summarize]
Observed variations by drink or technique: [facts]
Bartender experience and verified skills: [facts]
High-volume or high-risk drinks: [list]
Service schedule and available practice time: [facts]

Prioritize the smallest set of standards that will reduce the greatest quality, cost, speed, and guest risk. Include trainer demonstration, measured practice, blind recipe recall where appropriate, live representative observation, remediation for misses, and independent manager verification. Do not certify from attendance or time completed alone.
manager_check: Train the approved version and verify repeatable execution under representative service conditions.

title: BEVERAGE FEATURE / PROMOTION PROFITABILITY TEST
prompt:
Evaluate this proposed beverage feature or promotion before launch.

Drink and approved recipe: [details]
Recipe cost, selling price, and expected contribution: [data]
Target guest or occasion: [facts]
Expected units and timing: [range]
Inventory already on hand and any new one-use products: [data]
Prep, service, training, responsible-service, and POS requirements: [facts]

Identify the financial case, inventory risk, operational burden, training need, cannibalization risk, responsible-service guardrails, and evidence required to judge the test. Produce a launch/no-launch checklist plus keep/change/stop thresholds. Do not label added sales as profitable without considering product cost, labor, waste, and displaced sales.
manager_check: A feature must improve contribution and fit the operation; it is not useful merely because it is creative.

title: USABLE INVENTORY RECONCILIATION
prompt:
Convert this beverage count into usable inventory for the next order decision.

Physical count by full, open, partial, keg, case, or each: [data]
Approved open-container count method: [method]
Damaged, expired, spoiled, committed, quarantined, returned, or designated-for-disposal product: [data]
Transfers and count-unit definitions: [facts]

Calculate Usable On Hand = Physical On Hand - Unusable / Committed Product only where units are compatible. Flag mixed units, unsupported estimates, method changes, and high-risk counts requiring management verification. Produce a reconciliation table that preserves physical count, deductions, reason, usable amount, verifier, and unresolved question.
manager_check: Product can physically exist without being usable for normal ordering; never hide deductions inside the final number.

title: GRAVITY SMART ORDER BUILDER
prompt:
Build a beverage order from target need and usable inventory rather than memory or an empty shelf.

Approved normal par by item: [data]
Approved Temporary Target where applicable: [data and expiration]
Usable Inventory On Hand: [data]
Open purchase orders and delivery timing: [data]
Purchase unit, order minimum, budget guardrail, and known vendor issue: [facts]

Use Suggested Order = Target Need - Usable Inventory On Hand, then show any proposed Final Order adjustment separately with its reason. Round only according to the purchase unit and stated management rule. Flag fractional needs that do not justify an additional unit, duplicate open orders, items that no longer belong in the program, and decisions that require manager approval.
manager_check: Keep the mathematical suggestion separate from management’s approved adjustment so the decision remains visible.

title: TEMPORARY TARGET & EVENT RESET PLAN
prompt:
Create a controlled beverage inventory plan for this event or temporary demand exception.

Event, date, expected guests, and service window: [facts]
Featured beverages and expected mix: [data or range]
Normal pars and usable on hand: [data]
Delivery dates, storage limits, and substitutions: [facts]
Products affected beyond the obvious base spirit: [mixers / modifiers / wine / beer / garnishes / zero-proof]

Recommend Temporary Targets only where the evidence supports them, calculate suggested orders from usable on hand, identify cross-use and leftover risk, state the target’s expiration, and create a post-event reset review. Do not convert a one-time target into a permanent par without later evidence.
manager_check: The temporary target expires; it must not silently become the new normal.

title: RECEIVING, COST-CHANGE & CREDIT CLOSURE REVIEW
prompt:
Review this beverage delivery from ordered quantity through verified financial closure.

Purchase order: [ordered items / quantities / expected unit costs]
Receiving record: [delivered / short / substituted / damaged]
Invoice: [actual units / unit costs / fees]
Credits promised or returns: [facts]
Affected recipes, prices, pars, or future orders: [facts]

Identify quantity and invoice discrepancies, calculate cost changes where supported, show which changes must travel to recipe or pricing review, list credits still open, and assign the next action and verifier. Separate received, accepted, disputed, credited, and verified-closed status. Do not close a vendor credit merely because it was promised.
manager_check: Receiving is the second half of ordering, and a promised credit remains open until verified.

title: BEVERAGE VENDOR TOTAL-VALUE COMPARISON
prompt:
Compare these beverage vendors on total operating value, not unit price alone.

Quoted prices and package sizes: [data]
Minimums, delivery frequency, lead time, fill rate, shortages, substitutions, and emergency support: [data]
Credit handling, invoice accuracy, quality, availability, and administrative burden: [facts]
Restaurant demand, storage, cash, and continuity constraints: [facts]

Normalize comparable unit costs where the data supports it. Then score or summarize the operational tradeoffs without inventing weights. Identify which vendor is stronger for routine supply, high-risk items, emergency continuity, or negotiation, and state what evidence management still needs. Do not recommend the cheapest quote automatically.
manager_check: A lower price can cost more when minimums, shortages, credits, and service failure are included.

title: DEAD INVENTORY & COUNT-ACCURACY DECISION REVIEW
prompt:
Review this slow-moving beverage inventory without confusing a count problem with a product problem.

Current and prior counts with count method: [data]
Product value, menu reach, units sold, and last meaningful use: [data]
Purchases, transfers, waste, breakage, and known adjustments: [data]
Current status or proposed action: [facts]

First test count-unit consistency, open-container method, purchases, transfers, and recording accuracy. Then identify products that appear to be true dead or excess inventory. Recommend an evidence-based decision: keep, reduce par, cross-use, seasonal hold, approved depletion, legal return, substitute, or retire. State why and identify any conclusion that must wait for a verified recount.
manager_check: Verify the count before drawing a behavior or product conclusion; use responsible, lawful depletion methods only.

title: QUIET GRAVITY PREREQUISITE READINESS REVIEW
prompt:
Prepare a readiness discussion after a manager or management trainee reads Quiet Gravity.

Role and current responsibilities: [facts]
Five reflections or passages the reader identified: [paste or summarize]
Examples the reader connected to leadership behavior: [facts]
Questions, disagreement, or uncertainty: [details]
Owner/GM observations from the discussion: [facts]

Organize the discussion around self-awareness, authority, fairness, listening, repair, and responsibility. Identify what the reader understands, what needs clarification, and what behavior should be observed before or during training. Recommend Ready to proceed, Proceed with support, or Complete prerequisite work first. Do not infer private experiences, diagnose the reader, or require agreement with every passage.
manager_check: Use the reading to begin an evidence-based discussion; do not demand private disclosures or identical agreement.

title: BASELINE MANAGER READINESS DIAGNOSTIC
prompt:
Build a baseline manager-readiness diagnostic from the evidence below.

Current role and authorized duties: [facts]
Known strengths supported by evidence: [facts]
Known risks or development needs: [facts]
Two opening scenarios and responses: [details]
Recent observations, records, and operating conditions: [facts]

Classify each relevant capability as Ready, Ready with coaching, Developing, or Not yet applicable. Separate knowledge, judgment, observable behavior, and missing evidence. Recommend the smallest role-based learning path and the first representative workplace test. Do not treat confidence, tenure, popularity, or a single answer as proof of readiness.
manager_check: A baseline assigns development; it does not grant authority or become an employment decision by itself.

title: OWNER/GM TRAINER QUALIFICATION GATE
prompt:
Evaluate whether this owner or GM is ready to serve as the manager-readiness trainer.

Modules already studied: [list]
Calibration-scenario response and reasoning: [details]
Example of coaching an incomplete or unsafe answer: [details]
Understanding of trainee and trainer authority boundaries: [details]
Observed training behavior and evidence: [facts]

Test whether the trainer can explain the standard, recognize a responsible alternative answer, protect an independent attempt, coach without humiliation, distinguish evidence from opinion, and refuse to sign unobserved work. Recommend Ready to train, Ready with support, or Complete development before training, with the evidence required for the next decision.
manager_check: Position and experience do not automatically prove that an owner or GM is ready to train another manager.

title: ETHICAL USE OF AUTHORITY DECISION REVIEW
prompt:
Review this proposed management decision for ethical use of authority.

Decision and intended result: [details]
Manager's actual authority and limits: [facts]
People and standards affected: [facts]
Evidence supporting the decision: [facts]
Alternatives considered: [list]
Pressure, conflict of interest, favoritism, or retaliation risk: [facts or unknown]

Identify whether the decision is necessary, fair, consistent, explainable, reversible where appropriate, and within authority. Flag any use of power for convenience, punishment, image protection, or personal preference. Recommend proceed, revise, escalate, or stop, and state what must be documented and reviewed afterward. Do not supply legal conclusions.
manager_check: Authority should be used for the good of people and the operation, within lawful and defined boundaries.

title: DIGNITY, FAIRNESS & EMPLOYEE-TREATMENT REVIEW
prompt:
Review this employee-treatment situation using dignity, fairness, and evidence.

Situation and decision required: [facts]
Applicable standard or expectation: [text]
Employee's known conduct and relevant context: [facts]
How comparable situations were handled: [facts or unknown]
Support, coaching, accommodation, or escalation already considered: [details]

Separate facts from labels and assumptions. Test whether the process allowed the employee to be heard, protected privacy, avoided humiliation, applied a relevant standard consistently, and explained any different treatment. Identify missing evidence and recommend a respectful next step within the manager's authority. Flag HR, legal, safety, retaliation, discrimination, or accommodation concerns for qualified review.
manager_check: Equal dignity does not require identical outcomes; differences must rest on relevant facts and consistent standards.

title: EMPLOYEE CONCERN & NON-RETALIATION RESPONSE PLAN
prompt:
Prepare a safe management response to this employee concern.

Concern as reported, using only necessary details: [facts]
Immediate safety or operational risk: [facts]
Manager's authority and required escalation path: [facts]
Confidentiality limits and records required: [policy]
Any scheduling, discipline, evaluation, or treatment decisions that could appear retaliatory: [facts]

Draft the manager's first response, clarifying questions, immediate protections, documentation steps, escalation, and follow-up commitment. Separate what the manager knows from what requires investigation. Identify actions to pause or independently review to reduce retaliation risk. Do not investigate beyond authority, promise secrecy, reach a legal conclusion, or judge credibility from tone alone.
manager_check: A concern must be received without punishment, dismissal, forced disclosure, or a promise the manager cannot keep.

title: TRAINEE ANSWER & RESPONSIBLE-ALTERNATIVE REVIEW
prompt:
Evaluate this manager-trainee answer without forcing one scripted response.

Scenario and questions: [paste]
Trainee's independent answer and reasoning: [paste]
Best-supported answer from the instructor edition: [paste or summarize]
Critical standard, authority boundary, and required outcome: [facts]
Observed workplace evidence, if any: [facts]

Classify the answer as Strong and ready to test, Acceptable with coaching, Incomplete, or Unsafe. Explain what facts and standards the trainee protected, whether a different approach is still responsible, what is missing, and what would make the answer unsafe. Provide coaching questions rather than replacing the trainee's thinking. State the representative workplace evidence required before authorization.
manager_check: Judge the reasoning and protected standard, not whether the trainee copied the instructor's wording.

title: CRITICAL-FAILURE & EMPLOYMENT-BOUNDARY CHECK
prompt:
Review this manager-readiness result for critical failure and decision boundaries.

Scenario, task, or observation: [details]
Trainee response or behavior: [facts]
Applicable critical standard: [facts]
Immediate risk to people, safety, legality, dignity, money, or records: [facts]
Existing policy, HR process, and manager authority: [facts]

Determine whether the result is a coachable miss, a retest condition, a temporary authority restriction, or a critical failure requiring immediate escalation. Separate training decisions from scheduling, promotion, discipline, or termination decisions. State what may be decided now, what requires consultation, what evidence must be preserved, and what must not be inferred. Do not generate a final employment decision.
manager_check: Training evidence may inform management, but this workbook alone must not make an employment decision.

title: WORKPLACE VERIFICATION EVIDENCE QUALITY AUDIT
prompt:
Audit the quality of evidence offered for this manager capability.

Capability and approved standard: [details]
Representative operating conditions: [facts]
What was directly observed: [facts]
Prompts, coaching, assistance, or unusual conditions: [facts]
Records or outcomes supporting the observation: [details]
Reviewer identity, authority, and relationship to the work: [facts]

Judge whether the evidence is direct, representative, specific, current, independently verified, and sufficient for the stated authority. Identify contamination from coaching, hindsight, self-report, easy conditions, or missing records. Recommend authorize, authorize with limits, gather more evidence, or retest, and specify the next representative test.
manager_check: Attendance, discussion, confidence, and an unobserved signature do not prove workplace capability.

title: SYSTEM GAP VS INDIVIDUAL PERFORMANCE DIAGNOSIS
prompt:
Determine whether this recurring performance problem is primarily an individual capability gap, a system gap, or both.

Expected result and approved standard: [facts]
Observed misses across people, shifts, or conditions: [facts]
Training and verification completed: [facts]
Staffing, tools, workload, authority, information, and operating conditions: [facts]
Manager direction, follow-up, and known exceptions: [facts]

Map the evidence by person, process, standard, tool, staffing, authority, and environment. Identify the strongest supported cause, competing explanations, and missing evidence. Recommend what to repair in the system, what to coach or retest with the individual, who owns each action, and how the result will be verified. Do not assign blame merely because one person's name appears on the record.
manager_check: Do not coach or discipline a person for a failure created by an unclear standard, broken tool, staffing limit, or conflicting direction.

title: MANAGER READINESS CHECKPOINT DECISION
prompt:
Prepare a manager-readiness checkpoint decision after the assigned module group.

Modules completed: [list]
Knowledge and scenario results: [evidence]
Observed workplace demonstrations: [evidence]
Critical misses, coaching, retests, and unresolved system gaps: [facts]
Authority currently held and authority being considered: [facts]

Summarize demonstrated strengths, incomplete capabilities, unsafe conditions, and evidence limitations. Recommend Advance, Advance with limits and support, Hold for targeted development, or Return to an earlier module. Assign the smallest next action, owner, representative test, and review date. Do not advance from completed pages alone.
manager_check: A checkpoint controls progression; it is not a ceremony and should not be passed to preserve a schedule.

title: 30-60 DAY POST-TRAINING REASSESSMENT
prompt:
Build a targeted 30-60 day reassessment for this trained manager.

Original readiness decision and authorized limits: [facts]
Capabilities requiring follow-up: [list]
Since-training records, outcomes, incidents, and observations: [facts]
Changes in role, staffing, standards, or operating conditions: [facts]
Manager and owner/GM concerns: [facts]

Select only the capabilities and scenarios that need review. Include one independent response, one representative workplace observation, retained-behavior evidence, system-gap check, and a bidirectional review conversation. Recommend continue authority, continue with support, narrow authority, targeted retraining, or escalation, with owners and dates. Do not restart the full program unless the evidence justifies it.
manager_check: Follow-up must test retained behavior under real conditions, not repeat the original classroom conversation.

title: FINAL SCENARIO BANK, ASSIGNMENT & RETEST PLAN
prompt:
Build a final manager-readiness judgment event from the available scenario bank.

Manager role and likely decisions: [facts]
Completed learning path and remaining risks: [facts]
Available core scenarios: [list]
Available role-specific scenarios: [list]
Scenarios previously seen or coached: [list]
Critical standards and authority boundaries: [facts]

Assign 10 mandatory core scenarios plus 4-6 role-specific scenarios where the bank supports that structure. Balance people, safety, operations, judgment, communication, records, escalation, and follow-through. Keep unused scenarios reserved for retest. Produce an assignment sheet and scoring plan that evaluates facts, decision, authority, manager language, and record/follow-up. Do not reveal answer guidance before the independent attempt.
manager_check: Use enough varied scenarios to test judgment while reserving unused material for a valid retest.

title: DECISION PRE-MORTEM
prompt:
Pressure-test this proposed restaurant decision before implementation.

Decision, intended result, owner, and deadline: [facts]
Evidence supporting it: [facts]
People, systems, money, guests, and standards affected: [facts]
Known limits and assumptions: [facts]

Assume the decision failed six months from now. Identify the most plausible causes, people or standards harmed, hidden dependencies, early warning signs, and preventive controls. Separate high-impact risks from unlikely possibilities. Produce a short proceed/revise/pilot/stop recommendation, named controls, monitoring dates, and a recovery trigger. Do not invent facts or use imagined failure as evidence of misconduct.
manager_check: Use this before commitment; imagined failure is a planning tool, not proof that failure will occur.

title: OWNER-GM ALIGNMENT REVIEW
prompt:
Compare the owner's expectations with the GM's understanding of the role.

Owner's stated priorities, limits, and measures of success: [paste]
GM's stated priorities, limits, and measures of success: [paste]
Current decision rights and escalation rules: [facts]
Recent disagreements, overrides, or missed expectations: [facts]

Identify agreements, contradictions, silent assumptions, unclear authority, reporting gaps, and decisions that appear to have two owners or none. Draft an alignment agenda that ends with explicit decisions, owners, measures, communication rules, and a review date. Do not decide that one person is correct merely because of title.
manager_check: Agreement on goals is insufficient when authority, reporting, and decision ownership remain unclear.

title: CONFLICTING DIRECTION RESOLVER
prompt:
Resolve these conflicting restaurant directions.

Direction A, source, time, and stated reason: [facts]
Direction B, source, time, and stated reason: [facts]
Approved SOP, policy, safety rule, or current standard: [facts]
Immediate operating conditions and risk: [facts]
Employee or manager caught between the directions: [role]

Separate actual conflict from wording differences. Identify which authority or controlling standard applies, what must be paused, who must resolve the conflict, and what the affected person should do safely in the meantime. Draft a short clarification message and the record needed to prevent recurrence. Never override law, safety requirements, or approved policy through informal preference.
manager_check: Do not make an employee choose privately between conflicting authorities or standards.

title: FAVORITISM & CONSISTENCY AUDIT
prompt:
Audit this management pattern for favoritism and unsupported inconsistency.

Decisions being compared: [schedules / opportunities / coaching / discipline / recognition]
People, dates, and relevant circumstances: [de-identified facts]
Applicable standards and decision owners: [facts]
Documented reasons for differences: [facts or missing]

Compare like situations using job-related criteria. Identify supported differences, unexplained differences, incomplete records, and patterns requiring independent review. Recommend corrections to process, documentation, communication, or oversight without presuming unlawful discrimination or individual intent. Flag retaliation, discrimination, accommodation, or legal concerns for qualified review.
manager_check: Different outcomes may be fair only when relevant facts and standards explain the difference.

title: MANAGER BURNOUT & CAPACITY REVIEW
prompt:
Review this manager's workload and operating capacity.

Role, scheduled hours, and actual availability demands: [facts]
Decisions, tasks, reports, and people currently owned: [list]
Interruptions, coverage, vacancies, and recurring emergencies: [facts]
Delegation, backup capability, and recovery time: [facts]
Recent errors, delays, missed follow-up, or behavior changes: [facts]

Identify overload, decision bottlenecks, avoidable work, abandoned delegation, single-person dependencies, and risks to judgment or employee treatment. Recommend what to stop, delegate, simplify, schedule, back up, or escalate. Include immediate safety protection and a 14-day capacity reset. Do not diagnose health conditions or treat endurance as proof of readiness.
manager_check: This is an operating-capacity review, not a medical diagnosis.

title: EMPLOYEE WORKLOAD FAIRNESS REVIEW
prompt:
Review workload distribution across this restaurant team.

Roles, verified skills, availability, and authorized duties: [facts]
Difficult stations, closing duties, call-in coverage, training assignments, and schedule disruptions: [records]
Hours, recovery time, requested limits, and approved accommodations: [facts]
Business needs and staffing constraints: [facts]

Identify concentrated burdens, repeated inconvenience, invisible support work, skill-based reasons for differences, and gaps that records cannot explain. Recommend fair redistribution, cross-training, recognition, staffing, or manager review while protecting privacy. Do not infer motivation or recommend changes that violate availability, accommodation, safety, or policy.
manager_check: Fairness requires relevant evidence; it does not require every employee to receive identical work.

title: RUMOR, GOSSIP & TRUST REPAIR PLAN
prompt:
Prepare a response to a rumor or gossip problem affecting the restaurant.

What was directly reported or observed: [facts]
What remains unverified: [claims]
People, privacy, safety, or operations affected: [facts]
Relevant conduct, reporting, and escalation standards: [facts]

Separate verified information, legitimate employee concerns, harmful repetition, and unknowns. Recommend immediate communication, private fact-finding within authority, protections against retaliation, behavior expectations, escalation, and follow-up. Draft language that corrects the process without publishing private details or demanding silence about lawful concerns. Do not identify a source through speculation.
manager_check: Address workplace damage without repeating allegations unnecessarily or turning rumor into fact.

title: CHANGE-READINESS TEST
prompt:
Test whether this proposed restaurant change is ready for implementation.

Problem and intended result: [facts]
Proposed change and decision owner: [details]
Affected roles, systems, standards, guests, and records: [facts]
Training, tools, staffing, time, and budget available: [facts]
Pilot, measurement, rollback, and communication plan: [details]

Score readiness across clarity, authority, capacity, training, controlled documents, dependencies, risk, measurement, and sustainment. Identify blocking gaps and distinguish must-fix-before-launch items from manageable pilot risks. Recommend launch, limited pilot, revise, or hold, with owners and dates. Do not confuse announcement with installation.
manager_check: A good idea is not ready to launch until the operation can understand, support, and verify it.

title: POLICY EXCEPTION DECISION
prompt:
Evaluate this requested exception to a restaurant policy or standard.

Policy or standard and its purpose: [text]
Requested exception, reason, scope, and duration: [facts]
Requester and authorized decision owner: [roles]
People, safety, legal, financial, guest, and precedent risks: [facts]
Available alternatives: [list]

Determine whether the exception is necessary, within authority, consistent with controlling requirements, time-limited, and capable of being monitored. State approve/modify/deny/escalate, required safeguards, documentation, communication, expiration, and post-exception review. Flag legal, HR, food-safety, accessibility, or accommodation issues for qualified review.
manager_check: An exception must remain visible, authorized, limited, and reviewable so it does not silently become the standard.

title: MANAGER APOLOGY & REPAIR PREPARATION
prompt:
Help this manager prepare an accountable apology and repair conversation.

What the manager said, did, or failed to do: [facts]
Impact reported or observed: [facts]
Standard, promise, or responsibility missed: [facts]
Immediate correction already made: [facts]
Authority and privacy limits: [facts]

Draft a concise apology that acknowledges the specific action and impact, accepts responsibility without excuses, states the correction, invites appropriate input, and commits to follow-up. Add a repair plan with observable actions and a review date. Avoid admissions or promises beyond known facts and authority; flag matters requiring HR, legal, insurer, or senior-leader guidance.
manager_check: A useful apology names the harm and repair without demanding forgiveness or centering the manager's intentions.

title: RECOGNITION FAIRNESS & CREDIBILITY REVIEW
prompt:
Review this restaurant's recognition pattern for fairness and credibility.

Recognition given, by whom, and stated reasons: [records]
Relevant contributions and verified outcomes: [facts]
Employees, roles, shifts, and work that receive little visibility: [facts]
Current recognition criteria and opportunities: [facts]

Identify specific earned recognition, vague praise, repeated visibility bias, overlooked support work, and unequal access to recognition opportunities. Recommend clearer criteria, evidence sources, manager practices, and a balanced recognition plan. Do not rank employee worth, invent contributions, or disclose private performance information.
manager_check: Recognition should make valuable behavior visible without turning popularity or visibility into the standard.

title: SUCCESSION & SINGLE-POINT-OF-FAILURE REVIEW
prompt:
Identify restaurant work that depends too heavily on one person.

Critical duties, decisions, relationships, access, and knowledge: [list]
Current owners and verified backups: [facts]
Controlled instructions, records, and access protections: [facts]
Upcoming absences, turnover risks, or growth needs: [facts]

Map single-person dependencies by operational impact and urgency. Recommend documentation, cross-training, decision-right clarification, access controls, backup verification, and staged succession. Protect confidential access and preserve separation of duties. Do not recommend sharing passwords, bypassing controls, or removing appropriate specialist ownership.
manager_check: The goal is dependable continuity, not making one valuable employee easier to replace.

title: ETHICAL SALES-PRESSURE CHECK
prompt:
Review this sales contest, upselling expectation, quota, or promotion for ethical pressure.

Offer, target, incentive, and measurement method: [facts]
Products, prices, margins, and guest value: [facts]
Employee expectations and consequences: [facts]
Responsible-service, disclosure, accessibility, and service standards: [facts]

Identify legitimate selling behavior, coercive or misleading pressure, incentive distortion, fairness problems, operational burden, and risks to guest trust. Recommend proceed, revise, pilot, or stop, with approved language, guardrails, monitoring, and stop conditions. Do not encourage deceptive selling or treat every guest interaction as a sales failure.
manager_check: Sales growth is not acceptable when it depends on misleading guests, humiliating employees, or sacrificing service standards.

title: ANONYMOUS FEEDBACK PATTERN REVIEW
prompt:
Analyze this set of anonymous restaurant feedback responsibly.

Feedback entries with dates and necessary context: [de-identified text]
Known operating records or corroborating evidence: [facts]
Relevant standards and reporting channels: [facts]
Previous related concerns and actions: [facts]

Group recurring themes without guessing identities. Separate verifiable operational signals, serious allegations requiring escalation, opinions, isolated claims, and missing evidence. Recommend safe follow-up, independent fact checks, communication, protections against retaliation, and review dates. Do not expose writing-style clues or use AI to identify anonymous contributors.
manager_check: Anonymous feedback can reveal risk, but anonymity does not prove or disprove the underlying claim.

title: MEETING VALUE AUDIT
prompt:
Audit this restaurant's recurring meetings.

Meeting list, frequency, duration, participants, and purpose: [facts]
Recent agendas, decisions, action items, and completion rates: [records]
Information available through existing logs or reports: [facts]
Participant feedback and operating constraints: [facts]

Classify each meeting as keep, shorten, combine, redesign, replace with an existing record, or eliminate. Identify decisions that need live discussion, attendees who are necessary, preparation required, and follow-through controls. Produce a lean meeting rhythm and estimate time returned. Do not remove legally, contractually, or safety-required communication.
manager_check: A meeting earns its time by producing necessary understanding, decisions, ownership, or coordination.

title: MANAGER PROMISE & COMMITMENT TRACKER
prompt:
Build a control record for management promises and commitments.

Promises made to employees, guests, vendors, owners, or managers: [list]
Person responsible and person affected: [roles]
Date promised, due date, evidence, and current status: [facts]
Dependencies, authority limits, and changed conditions: [facts]

Separate commitments, intentions, requests, and unauthorized promises. Identify overdue or unclear commitments, reputational risk, and the next honest communication required. Produce a concise tracker with owner, due date, next action, verification, and closure status. Do not mark an item complete because a message was sent or because the original promise became inconvenient.
manager_check: A promise remains open until delivered, renegotiated honestly, or explicitly closed with the affected person.

title: OPERATIONAL CHANGE CONSEQUENCE REVIEW
prompt:
Trace the consequences of this proposed operational change across the restaurant.

Change, reason, owner, and intended benefit: [facts]
Affected role, station, process, tool, or standard: [facts]
Current baseline and known dependencies: [facts]
Time, staffing, training, technology, and financial constraints: [facts]

Map likely effects on labor, training, food safety, speed, quality, cleanliness, guest experience, employee workload, records, inventory, cash, and management follow-through. Identify required companion changes, new failure points, conflicts with controlled documents, and measures for a reversible pilot. Recommend proceed, revise, sequence, or stop without inventing impacts unsupported by the supplied facts.
manager_check: A local improvement can create a larger failure elsewhere when system connections are ignored.

title: WHAT ARE WE PRETENDING NOT TO KNOW? REVIEW
prompt:
Conduct a disciplined truth review of this restaurant or leadership team.

Recurring problems, exceptions, complaints, and missed commitments: [facts]
Relevant operating and people records: [data]
What employees, managers, guests, or vendors repeatedly report: [de-identified facts]
Explanations and actions already attempted: [facts]

Identify truths supported by repeated evidence, important questions still open, contradictions between stated standards and actual behavior, and issues being renamed instead of resolved. Separate evidence from suspicion. Recommend the first truth to face, decision owner, immediate protection, smallest corrective action, verification measure, and review date. Do not diagnose motives or turn anonymous claims into established fact.
manager_check: Use this to face supported operating truth, not to accuse people or manufacture certainty.

title: CONTROL & PAPERWORK BURDEN REVIEW
prompt:
Audit the restaurant's current forms, logs, checklists, trackers, meetings, and recurring reports.

Control name, purpose, owner, user, frequency, and review method: [list]
Decisions actually made from each control: [facts]
Completion time, duplication, missed use, and complaints: [facts]
Legal, safety, accounting, payroll, insurance, or policy requirements: [facts]

Identify required controls, high-value controls, duplicates, unused records, excessive frequency, fields nobody reviews, and controls that could be combined or retired. Recommend keep, simplify, combine, reduce frequency, replace, or retire, with decision owners and safeguards. Do not remove an authoritative or risk-critical record merely because it is inconvenient.
manager_check: A control earns its place only when its decision value exceeds the burden of completing and reviewing it.

title: MINIMUM-NECESSARY DATA & PRIVACY REVIEW
prompt:
Review this restaurant record, workflow, or system for minimum-necessary data use.

Business purpose and authorized users: [facts]
Fields collected, source, and frequency: [list]
Employee, guest, payment, health, identity, or confidential information involved: [facts]
Storage, access, sharing, retention, and deletion practices: [facts]
Applicable policy and authoritative requirements: [facts]

Identify unnecessary fields, excessive access, risky free-text collection, avoidable identifiers, unclear retention, uncontrolled copies, and missing ownership. Recommend minimize, mask, restrict, separate, retain, archive, or securely delete within policy and law. Do not request passwords, full payment-card data, or unnecessary personal information.
manager_check: Collect and expose only the information necessary for the authorized operating purpose.

title: UNKNOWN-ISSUE & BLIND-SPOT DISCOVERY
prompt:
Search these restaurant records for important issues management has not already named.

Time period and operating context: [facts]
Sales, labor, food cost, waste, guest, training, maintenance, safety, cash, and people signals available: [data]
Known issues and actions already open: [list]
Missing, delayed, inconsistent, or unusually quiet records: [facts]

Identify anomalies, unexpected relationships, repeated exceptions, missing expected activity, sudden changes, and areas where the absence of evidence may itself require a check. Rank only evidence-supported investigation questions by potential impact and urgency. State what record or observation would confirm or reject each question. Do not label an anomaly as misconduct, causation, or proof.
manager_check: This review searches for unsupported assumptions and unexplained patterns; it does not manufacture problems.

title: PILOT-TO-OPERATIONAL MATURITY GATE
prompt:
Decide whether this restaurant tool, process, or system is ready to move beyond controlled pilot status.

Pilot purpose, scope, owner, locations, roles, and dates: [facts]
Completion, adoption, outcome, exception, and corrective-action evidence: [data]
Training, documentation, access, backup, and review controls: [facts]
Failures, workarounds, unresolved risks, and user feedback: [facts]

Evaluate clarity, usability, adoption, result quality, evidence integrity, ownership, scalability, failure recovery, and sustainment. Recommend remain in development, extend pilot, approve with limits, or move to operational status. Specify blocking gaps, approval owner, controlled version, review date, and rollback trigger. Do not promote status to meet a deadline or because no complaint was recorded.
manager_check: A successful demonstration is not enough; operational maturity requires repeatable use, ownership, evidence, and recovery from failure.

title: CROSS-SYSTEM SIGNAL & CAUSATION CHECK
prompt:
Review this possible relationship between restaurant results across systems.

Signals, definitions, sources, and time periods: [data]
Observed timing and pattern: [facts]
Relevant changes in price, hours, staffing, menu, weather, events, equipment, or operations: [facts]
Known data-quality limits and missing comparison periods: [facts]

Test timing, unit consistency, alternative explanations, lag effects, seasonality, and whether the relationship repeats under comparable conditions. Separate observation, plausible explanation, testable hypothesis, and supported conclusion. Recommend the smallest safe test or additional evidence needed before action. Do not claim causation or individual fault from correlation alone.
manager_check: Signals moving together can guide investigation, but correlation alone does not establish cause.

title: FEEDBACK-TO-SYSTEM IMPROVEMENT CONTROL
prompt:
Convert this collection of restaurant feedback into controlled improvement decisions.

Feedback from employees, managers, guests, vendors, or auditors: [de-identified entries]
Affected standard, tool, process, or system: [facts]
Frequency, severity, evidence, and operating context: [facts]
Previous responses and current owner: [facts]

Group repeated themes while preserving meaningful disagreement. Separate misunderstanding, training need, usability problem, system defect, isolated preference, risk report, and improvement opportunity. Recommend clarify, train, correct, test, defer, reject, or escalate, with reason, owner, due date, verification, and response to the people affected. Do not promise every suggestion will be adopted or expose confidential identities.
manager_check: Feedback becomes valuable when it is classified, decided, owned, tested, and closed visibly.

title: COMPLAINT THEME CLASSIFICATION
prompt: Using only the complaint records I provide, group the concerns into stable restaurant categories such as service, food quality, accuracy, speed, facility, policy, expectation, payment, safety, or conduct. Separate reported facts from verified facts. Do not decide blame. Show any records that do not fit cleanly and explain what additional fact a manager should verify.
manager_check: Classification organizes evidence; it does not decide blame or turn a guest report into a verified fact.

title: REPEAT-CAUSE PATTERN REVIEW
prompt: Review these guest concern records by shift, daypart, station, item, manager response, and failure type. Identify repeated patterns that are supported by the data, distinguish frequency from severity, and list evidence gaps. Do not assume one employee caused a system pattern.
manager_check: A repeated pattern is an investigation target; do not assign individual cause without supporting evidence.

title: RECOVERY FOLLOW-UP DRAFT
prompt: From the verified facts and the recovery action already approved by the manager, draft a short, calm guest follow-up message. Acknowledge the experience, state only verified facts, explain the approved next step, avoid legal admissions or unsupported promises, and leave any unresolved authority question for the manager.
manager_check: The manager controls facts, authority, compensation, and final wording; AI may only draft from approved information.

title: RECOVERY ROLE-PLAY BUILDER
prompt: Using this restaurant's approved service standard, recovery authority matrix, and escalation rules, create five realistic role-play scenarios for managers. Vary severity, guest emotion, operating pressure, and whether the first attempted recovery works. For each scenario, provide evaluator questions rather than a single scripted answer.
manager_check: Role-play should test judgment against the restaurant's real authority and escalation standards, not invent new policy.

title: DIRECT + ONLINE FEEDBACK COMPARISON
prompt: Compare these direct guest complaints and online reviews for repeated themes without exposing unnecessary guest information. Show which themes appear in both sources, which appear only in one source, and which claims still require internal verification before the restaurant changes a standard.
manager_check: Protect guest privacy and verify claims internally before changing a standard or treating public feedback as established fact.

title: CORRECTIVE-ACTION BUILDER
prompt: Turn this verified repeated guest-experience cause into the smallest useful corrective-action plan. Include the truth/evidence, cost or risk, one operating change, named owner, due date, training or communication needed, verification evidence, and a stop/revise/standardize decision point. Do not create extra paperwork unless it adds control value.
manager_check: Use the smallest control that addresses a verified cause; paperwork is not a substitute for correction or verification.

title: GUEST RECOVERY METRICS
prompt: Using the totals I provide, calculate complaints per 100 guests, manager acknowledgment time, first-contact resolution rate, follow-up completion rate, repeat-theme rate, and verified guest-return rate where the data supports them. Show each formula, denominator, missing-data limitation, and what management question each number can actually answer.
manager_check: Verify every numerator, denominator, and definition; a metric is useful only when the underlying records support it.

title: PRE-SHIFT RECOVERY COACHING NOTE
prompt: Create a five-minute pre-shift coaching note around this one guest-recovery standard. Include what employees should notice, what they may handle themselves, when to involve a manager, one short practice question, and why the standard protects the guest and the team. Do not invent authority limits that are not supplied.
manager_check: Use the restaurant's approved recovery standard and authority limits; do not let a coaching note silently create policy.

title: AUTHORITY-MATRIX GAP REVIEW
prompt: Review this restaurant's recovery authority matrix for ambiguity, overlap, missing escalation points, or situations where employees may wait for approval unnecessarily. Return questions for the owner/GM to resolve. Do not set compensation amounts or final policy yourself.
manager_check: AI may expose ambiguity; only authorized leadership sets recovery limits, compensation authority, and final policy.

title: WEEKLY GUEST EXPERIENCE REVIEW
prompt: Using these open cases, closed cases, online reviews, repeat patterns, follow-up commitments, and corrective actions, draft a concise weekly guest-experience meeting agenda. Separate case closure from cause closure. End with the three decisions that require a named owner, due date, and verification evidence.
manager_check: Closing a guest case is not the same as correcting the cause; keep ownership, due dates, and verification visible.

title: PERSONALIZER PRODUCTION & PROOF BRIEF
prompt: Build a production brief for this existing Gravity item before I personalize or print it. Material: [form/poster/checklist/sign/QR item]. Restaurant/company name: [name]. Store/unit number and location: [data]. Logo/brand requirements: [data]. Approved wording: [text]. QR destination: [URL or none]. Finished size/format: [spec]. Quantity/finish: [spec]. Return a field-by-field personalization checklist, proofing checklist, QR test checklist, and final production questions. Do not rewrite controlled operating content unless I explicitly authorize a wording change.
manager_check: Personalization changes presentation and local identity; it must not silently change the controlled standard, legal language, or QR destination.

title: DOCUMENT STUDIO BUILDER SELECTION & SOURCE CHECKLIST
prompt: Choose the best Gravity Document Studio builder for this management need and tell me what source information I should gather before I start. Need: [describe]. Intended audience: [employees/managers/candidates/other]. Required decisions or approvals: [known items]. Existing policies/forms: [list]. Identify the most appropriate builder, any closely related builder I should not confuse it with, the minimum source records needed, privacy-sensitive fields to avoid unless necessary, and any official or provider-specific form that should stay outside Document Studio.
manager_check: Use Document Studio to organize restaurant-created documents; verify changing government, legal, payroll, insurance, and provider-specific requirements at the authoritative source.

title: DOCUMENT STUDIO DRAFT COMPLETENESS & POLICY-BOUNDARY REVIEW
prompt: Review this draft restaurant document before it is issued. Draft: [paste text with unnecessary personal information removed]. Intended purpose: [purpose]. Approved policy/source: [reference]. Check for missing owners, dates, definitions, acknowledgments, approval fields, escalation points, conflicting language, accidental promises, vague enforcement language, and places where the draft creates policy beyond the approved source. Return only the questions and edits management should resolve before release.
manager_check: AI may improve completeness and clarity; authorized leadership must approve policy, employment terms, discipline, pay, legal language, and final use.

title: SHIFT LAB AVAILABILITY, QUALIFICATION & COVERAGE CONFLICT REVIEW
prompt: Review this proposed weekly schedule using the same decision logic a manager should apply in Gravity Shift Lab. Forecast/coverage need: [data]. Employee availability and approved time off: [data]. Qualified/cross-trained sections: [data]. Proposed shifts: [data]. Max-hour or overtime limits: [rules]. Identify hard availability conflicts, unqualified assignments, uncovered sections/dayparts, overtime risk, closing/opening concerns, and employees who appear overloaded or underused. Give me questions to resolve before publishing; do not assume unavailable or unqualified employees can work.
manager_check: The schedule must follow verified availability, qualifications, wage/hour requirements, local rules, and management judgment; optimization never overrides a hard constraint.

title: SHIFT LAB CALL-OUT FIND-COVERAGE DECISION
prompt: Help me work a call-out using a Find Coverage approach. Open shift: [date/time/section]. Required qualifications: [requirements]. Candidate availability: [data]. Existing scheduled hours: [data]. Overtime/max-hour limits: [rules]. Contact/privacy rules: [what a delegated scheduler may see]. Rank candidates by qualification, availability, schedule fit, overtime risk, and operational impact. Show why each person is or is not a reasonable contact. Do not expose private pay or contact information beyond the access I specify.
manager_check: Coverage matching supports the manager; it does not authorize schedule changes, overtime, contact disclosure, or qualification overrides by itself.

title: SHIFT LAB PUBLISH, REVISION & EMPLOYEE-PRIVACY AUDIT
prompt: Audit this schedule before and after publication. Manager schedule data: [data]. Employee-facing fields: [fields]. Proposed QR/share method: [method]. Current published version: [version]. Changes since publication: [list]. Confirm that the employee-facing copy excludes wage rates, labor dollars, private phone numbers, manager-only notes, and other restricted fields; identify whether the schedule should be marked Published or Revised; and produce a concise change-log entry with date, change, owner, reason, and republish requirement.
manager_check: Published schedules need version control and minimum-necessary disclosure; a convenient QR link is not permission to expose manager-only information.

title: FOUNDRY MASTER-TO-LOCAL REVISION RECONCILIATION
prompt: Compare this restaurant working SOP with the current Gravity master without overwriting either one. Gravity master: [text/version]. Local working SOP: [text/version]. Local authority or equipment differences: [notes]. Separate changes into intentional local customization, likely drift, obsolete wording, unresolved requirements, and items needing current authority verification. Then propose a revision plan showing what to keep, what to investigate, what to retrain, and what evidence should be saved with the revision.
manager_check: A master/local comparison exposes differences; management must verify local law, equipment, policy, and operating reality before approving a revised SOP.

title: FOUNDRY BINDER DEPLOYMENT & ONE-PAGE PLAN
prompt: Turn this approved SOP set into a practical deployment plan. SOPs/stations: [list]. Audiences: [roles]. Detailed versions available: [yes/no]. One-page operational versions needed: [stations]. Required approvals: [owners]. Training evidence: [records]. Build a binder/section order, identify which SOPs deserve one-page station copies, assign owners and review frequencies, list unresolved fields that must be closed before issue, and create a rollout sequence that avoids dumping the entire binder on the team at once.
manager_check: A binder is useful only when employees can find the current approved standard, understand it, train to it, and know when it changed.

title: CATERING / BANQUET EVENT COMMAND PLAN
prompt: Build an event command plan from this catering or banquet information: [event details], guest count/timing: [data], menu/service format: [data], contract/BEO commitments: [data], payment/deposit status: [data], load-out/transport needs: [data], site constraints: [data], staffing: [data]. Identify handoffs, critical times, temperature/transport controls, setup readiness, payment or scope questions, replenishment responsibilities, breakdown/return reconciliation, and the manager decision points most likely to fail if ownership is unclear.
manager_check: Use the approved event order, contract, food-safety requirements, payment terms, and site rules as the source of truth; AI does not change a guest commitment.

title: MOBILE UNIT / TEMPORARY EVENT READINESS MAP
prompt: Create a pre-departure and site-readiness map for this food truck, mobile unit, or temporary event. Location/event: [details]. Menu: [items]. Commissary support: [plan]. Fresh water/wastewater capacity: [data]. Propane/fuel/generator: [data]. Handwashing/warewashing: [plan]. Permits/local conditions: [known requirements]. Separate what must be verified before departure, on arrival, during service, and on return to the commissary. Flag any capacity or safety dependency that could stop service.
manager_check: Mobile and temporary operations depend on local regulatory, fire, utility, food-safety, and commissary requirements; verify them before operating.

title: DRIVE-THRU / CURBSIDE PEAK FLOW CONTROL REVIEW
prompt: Review this drive-thru, curbside, or high-volume off-premise plan for a peak period. Demand by 15/30-minute interval: [data]. Order channels: [channels]. Staging space: [limits]. Staffing/deployment: [data]. Accuracy and handoff steps: [process]. Speed targets: [targets]. Identify queue bottlenecks, lane/curbside collision points, staging overload, accuracy risk, payment/handoff confusion, and when digital-order throttling or a recovery trigger should be considered. Return a short peak-control plan with measurable checkpoints.
manager_check: Speed is not the only target; preserve safety, order accuracy, food quality, guest identification, and approved channel rules.

title: COMMISSARY TRANSFER CHAIN-OF-CONTROL PLAN
prompt: Review this central-production or inter-unit transfer process. Product/batch: [data]. Producing unit: [location]. Receiving unit: [location]. Batch/label codes: [data]. Cooling/holding requirements: [standards]. Transport time/temperature: [data]. Transfer authorization: [record]. Container/tote return: [process]. Map custody from production through receipt, flag traceability or cold/hot-chain gaps, identify required receiving checks, and show what must reconcile between yield, transfer quantity, and receipt.
manager_check: Inter-unit movement does not reduce food-safety, traceability, labeling, or receiving requirements; verify the applicable standard at both locations.

title: BUFFET / SELF-SERVICE EXPOSURE & HOLDING REVIEW
prompt: Audit this buffet, salad bar, carving station, action station, or self-service setup. Menu/items: [list]. Holding methods/temperatures: [data]. Replenishment method: [process]. Utensil/barrier setup: [details]. Guest-contact risks: [observations]. Leftover policy: [standard]. Identify opening defects, monitoring points, contamination triggers, small-batch/replenishment opportunities, utensil or barrier failures, and closing disposition decisions. Return a manager observation route and escalation triggers.
manager_check: Self-service controls must follow current food-safety requirements and the restaurant’s approved disposition rules; appearance or speed never overrides contamination control.

title: SPECIALIZED PROCESS CONTROL & DEVIATION REVIEW
prompt: Review this specialized food process using only the approved plan and records I provide. Process: [ROP/sous vide/cook-chill/non-continuous cooking/curing/fermentation/acidification/other]. Approved HACCP/variance or authority requirements: [source]. Critical limits/steps: [data]. Monitoring records: [data]. Deviation: [if any]. Identify missing monitoring, label/date-control gaps, deviations from the approved process, required hold/escalation questions, and records management must verify before product is released or the process continues.
manager_check: Do not invent critical limits, corrective actions, or regulatory approvals; use the current approved plan and competent regulatory/food-safety authority.

title: RAW / UNDERCOOKED & HIGH-RISK INGREDIENT CONTROL REVIEW
prompt: Review controls for this raw, undercooked, or unusually high-risk ingredient/service. Ingredient/menu item: [item]. Supplier/source records: [data]. Required tags/certificates or parasite-destruction evidence: [records]. Storage/identity controls: [process]. Consumer advisory/label requirement: [approved wording]. Preparation/service controls: [steps]. Flag missing traceability, identity mixing, warning/advisory gaps, unsafe assumptions, and records that must be retained or verified before service.
manager_check: High-risk ingredients require current source, food-safety, and regulatory verification; AI cannot approve a supplier, advisory, treatment, or raw/undercooked service practice.

title: THIRD-PARTY DELIVERY / VIRTUAL-BRAND HANDOFF CONTROL
prompt: Review this third-party delivery, ghost-kitchen, or virtual-brand flow. Platforms/brands: [list]. Menu availability sync: [process]. Order acceptance/staging: [steps]. Driver identity/release method: [method]. Tamper-evident packaging: [standard]. Delayed/missing driver rules: [rules]. Identify cross-brand mix-up risk, stale menu availability, package/label mismatch, chain-of-custody breaks, delayed pickup exposure, and platform-outage backup steps. Return the minimum checkpoints for a manager to observe during a rush.
manager_check: Marketplace convenience does not transfer responsibility for food quality, correct order identity, approved packaging, or the restaurant’s release controls.

title: DRAFT & SPECIALTY BEVERAGE HIGH-CONTROL AUDIT
prompt: Audit this specialty beverage system or batch against its approved standard. System/product: [draft beer/CO2/nitro/batch cocktail/frozen beverage/wine preservation/espresso/cold brew/other]. Recipe/settings: [standard]. Cleaning/sanitation record: [data]. Pressure/time/temperature/shelf-life controls: [data]. Quality issue: [observations]. Separate product-quality problems from equipment, cleaning, recipe, labeling, storage, or safety problems and identify the evidence needed before changing settings or serving the product.
manager_check: Use manufacturer instructions, approved recipes, alcohol-service rules, sanitation standards, and trained technical support where required; do not improvise gas or equipment settings.

title: UNCOMMON EQUIPMENT / UTILITY FAILURE CONTINUITY PLAN
prompt: Build a continuity plan for this uncommon equipment or utility problem. Asset/system: [grease interceptor/backflow/fire suppression/hood/generator/refrigeration/ice/water treatment/drain/lift/other]. Failure signs: [facts]. Current service status: [data]. Product/food-safety impact: [data]. Building/employee impact: [data]. Vendor/authority contacts: [roles]. Separate immediate shutdown/containment questions, product decisions, service coordination, documentation, safe restart/recommissioning, and cross-system handoffs.
manager_check: Equipment and utility failures can create life-safety, food-safety, fire, plumbing, and code risks; follow qualified service and applicable authority requirements before restart.

title: REGIONAL DISASTER CONTINUITY RESOURCE PRIORITIZATION
prompt: Help management prioritize operations during this regional disruption. Hazard: [flood/smoke/civil access restriction/hazmat/grid failure/water/ice/supply disruption/other]. Affected locations: [units]. People/accountability status: [data]. Utilities: [status]. Refrigeration/product status: [data]. Supply routes: [status]. Safe access: [facts]. Rank immediate life-safety and employee-welfare needs, product/utility controls, menu reduction or closure questions, communication responsibilities, and the evidence required before reopening or recommissioning.
manager_check: Regional emergencies require current public-authority, utility, emergency, and food-safety information; business continuity never outranks life safety.

title: DONATION / REUSABLE / SUSTAINABILITY CONTROL REVIEW
prompt: Review this food-donation, recycling, composting, used-oil, reusable-container, or refillable-container program. Program: [type]. Eligible materials/products: [rules]. Storage/segregation: [process]. Cooling/sanitation where applicable: [standard]. Pickup/return verification: [process]. Vendor/agency records: [data]. Identify contamination, misidentification, traceability, pest, chemical, sanitation, or reporting gaps and separate operational improvement from claims that require legal/regulatory verification.
manager_check: Sustainability goals do not override food safety, sanitation, waste handling, vendor, donation, or local regulatory requirements.

title: LARGE EVENT / SEASONAL CROWD READINESS PLAN
prompt: Build a readiness plan for this unusual demand event. Event: [festival/stadium/holiday/group/VIP/buyout/late-night/other]. Forecast and timing waves: [data]. Service area/capacity: [limits]. Staffing: [data]. Production/holding: [plan]. Weather or outdoor risks: [data]. Security/access constraints: [data]. Identify demand triggers, deployment changes, production limits, crowd-flow controls, weather shutdown points, communication owners, and closeout/recovery work. Show which assumptions need confirmation before the plan is final.
manager_check: Crowd and event plans must respect occupancy, weather, security, alcohol, labor, food-safety, and local event requirements; confirm current limits with the responsible authority.

title: MULTI-UNIT OPENING / TEMPORARY LEADERSHIP READINESS REVIEW
prompt: Review readiness for this new-unit opening, soft opening, grand opening, temporary manager assignment, inter-unit manager coverage, acquisition, or restart. Unit/event: [context]. Current standards/version: [data]. Leadership/decision rights: [data]. Staffing/training: [data]. Vendor/equipment/permit readiness: [data]. Open issues: [list]. Separate launch blockers from monitor-after-opening items, flag unclear temporary authority, identify cross-unit SOP/version risks, and produce a stabilization checklist for the first operating days.
manager_check: Temporary leadership and new-unit pressure do not change decision rights, controlled standards, training requirements, or approval authority unless leadership explicitly changes them.

title: DIGITAL ORDERING & DATA-CONTINUITY OUTAGE PLAN
prompt: Build an outage and recovery plan for this restaurant technology dependency. System: [online ordering/QR ordering/gift card/payment terminal/marketplace/connected equipment/data backup/other]. Failure mode: [facts]. What still works: [data]. Offline/manual backup: [process]. Credentials/access owners: [roles]. Critical data/SOPs available offline: [yes/no]. Identify safe fallback steps, orders/payments that must be reconciled later, credential or tamper concerns, guest communication needs, backup/restore verification, and the exact point where the issue becomes a security or privacy escalation.
manager_check: Do not request or paste passwords, payment-card data, authentication secrets, or sensitive breach details into AI; use authorized IT/payment/security procedures.

title: GRAB-AND-GO / AUTOMATED / UNATTENDED SERVICE CONTROL REVIEW
prompt: Audit this grab-and-go, locker, kiosk, vending, meal-kit, or unattended pickup operation. Products: [list]. Label/date instructions: [data]. Display/locker/vending temperatures: [data]. Replenishment/rotation: [process]. Kiosk/manual backup: [process]. Security/abandoned-order rules: [standard]. Identify label, temperature, rotation, release, accessibility, outage, security, and product-withdrawal gaps. Return a manager inspection route and the records that should prove control.
